title: Drift-aware rollback orchestrator for multi-metric canaries
creator: Lina Chen
description: Build a rollout-side controller that triggers automated rollbacks for canary/A-B/shadow deployments using multi-metric SLO reasoning. Unlike simple threshold gates, this ticket implements drift-aware, cohort-resilient decision logic that adapts thresholds based on traffic composition, recent baseline drift, and token-cost budget exposure. The controller will provide configurable hysteresis, simulated test runs, and an operator-facing advisory mode (warn-only) before enforcement.
acceptance_criteria: Controller evaluates latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, token cost per request, and throughput concurrently and computes a unified risk score
Risk score mapping is configurable per project: weight vector and hysteresis window editable via rollout policy config
Controller supports cohort scoping (region, customer tier, route) and computes cohort baselines against historical windows to avoid false positives from traffic shifts
Automated rollback action performs a safe evacuation (traffic backfill to baseline or compatible variant) and emits a detailed incident event with metrics and attribution
Warn-only mode exposes advisory recommendations in Console and Slack without affecting traffic
Simulated canary replays (shadow) available: operator can run a dry-run on historical traffic to validate thresholds before real rollout
Integration tests covering an alert-injection harness that simulates gradual latency drift and a cost-surge scenario
Telemetry surfaced to Console: risk score time series, contributing signals, cohort membership, and rollback audit trail
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight risk scoring function: normalized z-score per metric with optional Bayesian smoothing to handle low-sample cohorts
Use adaptive thresholds: baseline percentile + delta where baseline computed from rolling 7d window with decay for relevance
Provide budget-aware override: when token-cost increases and project monthly budget remaining < X%, apply conservative rollback bias
Integrate with rollout engine API: provide /evaluate and /enforce endpoints; ensure idempotency and rate-limit enforcement
Add feature flag gating and a warn-only rollout flag so we can ramp the controller across orgs
Expose tuning knobs in Console (weights, hysteresis period, cohort selectors) and store config in rollout-policy proto
testing_plan: Unit tests for risk scoring math with deterministic inputs
Property tests for hysteresis and debouncing logic under noisy signals
E2E in staging: run canary with injected error-rate spike and verify rollback occurs and traffic is restored to baseline variant
Cost-surge scenario: synthetic workload that doubles token/sec for 10 minutes; verify budget-aware flag triggers earlier rollbacks when budget low
Chaos test: transient DB latency on metric pipeline should not cause immediate rollback — confirm noise filtering works
Simulated replay harness: run historic traffic window through controller in dry-run and assert advisory matches expected policy decisions
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): library + unit tests behind feature flag; code review and canary in internal org
Phase 1 (staging): enable warn-only for small set of teams; collect advisory telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (limited enforce): enable enforcement for non-critical routes with conservative defaults; run manual review after each rollback for 48h
Phase 3 (org-wide): enable enforcement with tuned defaults and UI controls; 30-day monitoring and postmortem checklist
Fallback: manual kill switch tied to paging schedule and ops runbook
